messages:
katie: Heads-up, bringing quasar-embed-3b into staging today. Converted to int8 per-channel for cost checks. Quick smoke looked fine but some signals worry me (short-query recall@1/10 delta).

alex: thanks — can you paste the small eval summary? numbers + dataset slices pls.

katie: sure. full run link: https://dash.internal/redwood/embeds/quasar-3b/staging (perm)

katie: embed-bot posted initial summary: see below.

embed-bot: EVAL SUMMARY (quasar-embed-3b · int8-perchannel)
- global recall@1: 0.764 (baseline float16: 0.779)
- recall@10: 0.918 (baseline: 0.941)
- avg cosine shift (random sample): 0.028
- silhouette score (k=100): 0.112 (baseline: 0.147)
- UMAP cluster separability metric: decreased 12%
- long-tail (freq<5) recall@1: 0.48 -> 0.41
- short-queries (<8 tokens) recall@1: 0.81 -> 0.77

nishant: those silhouette / cluster drops are non-trivial. Did you stratify by query length, language, and dataset cohort?

katie: yes, the eval already splits by: short/medium/long, top-cohort (SaaS docs), faq-style, multilingual (en/es/fr). Biggest regression is short + long-tail.

mike: hmm. int8 per-channel usually ok for generative models, but embeddings can be sensitive to centroid drift. Do we have centroid-wise mean shift per-layer?

nishant: I pulled layerwise stats. quick snippet below:
```
# summary script output (mean cos diff per layer)
layer_0: 0.0012
layer_4: 0.0028
layer_8: 0.0115  <-- biggest
layer_10: 0.0091
pooler: 0.0279
```

nishant: pooler shift at ~0.028 matches embed-bot cosine shift. suggests quantization error accumulating in final projection.

alex: can you upload a UMAP PNG of short-queries vs baseline? want to see if cluster collapse or just drift.

katie: uploaded 2 images to the run. Short-query UMAP shows tighter, overlapping clusters for several labels — looks like decreased inter-cluster margin.

mike: ok. hypothesis: per-channel int8 on final projection + layernorm rounding => reduced angular separability for short, sparse tokens. Two experiments to try: 1) per-tensor quant on the final projection (less params, but might reduce noise), 2) keep final proj in float16 (mixed precision) and quantize rest.

eva: also try using symmetric vs asymmetric quant params; asymmetric can bias centroids. I can try a micro-run with symmetric-only quant for the pooler.

katie: good plan. Also thinking of running a stratified holdout with heavier sampling on long-tail (freq<5 bucket) and short-queries so we get stable stats. Current run had small N in those slices.

nishant: schedule: eva, can you run a 10k-sample holdout focusing 50% long-tail, 30% short, 20% random? Use same prompt set as baseline. Script: 
```
python eval/emb_eval.py --model quasar-embed-3b-int8 --holdout-file holdout_quasar_stratified.json --k 10 --cohorts longtail,short,random --out=quasar_int8_strat.json
```

eva: starting that now. will try both pooler-fp16 and symmetric-only pooler quant variants. ETA ~45m.

embed-bot: note: runspace quota will auto-scale but estimates +1h wall time for both variants.

alex: also please capture recall curve vs distance threshold and per-cohort silhouette. If pooler-fp16 fixes recall but not cost enough, we can try 6-bit on other layers (masked) later.

mike: minor request — add kmeans-run stability check (seeded 5 runs) and report cluster assignment overlap (ARI). If quantization changes cluster assignments widely that's a concern for downstream search performance.

katie: added to the list.

nishant: if eva's runs confirm pooler-fp16 restores recall within 1% of baseline, I suggest we keep pooler FP16 in production int8 bundle for now and revisit tighter quantization later. We should also add an automated gate: if long-tail recall@1 drops >2% vs baseline, fail canary.

katie: agreed. I'll draft the gating rule and add to the rollout config.

eva: quick update — micro-run finished for symmetric-only pooler quant: recall@10 improved from 0.918 -> 0.932 (baseline 0.941). long-tail recall@1 improved to 0.449. still below baseline but closer.

eva: starting pooler-fp16 run now.

alex: thanks. can you attach the eval JSON when done and tag me? @alex

katie: tagging product for visibility after we have final numbers — might affect on-device cost vs accuracy tradeoffs. cc @product-ops

mike: also worth running a small online A/B with sampled traffic (non-critical route) to check downstream QA (reranking + hits@topk). We can use 2% traffic to int8 bundle with pooler-fp16 if eva's numbers look good.

katie: putting A/B playbook in the staging run doc. will coordinate with infra for canary rollout.

embed-bot: pooler-fp16 run complete (summary): recall@1: 0.772 (baseline 0.779), recall@10: 0.939 (baseline 0.941), silhouette(k=100): 0.142, long-tail recall@1: 0.476

katie: nice — pooler-fp16 almost restores to float16 for most metrics and cost savings still material (~28% lower token cost).

nishant: looks acceptable. next steps: 1) add canary gate for long-tail recall, 2) run 3 seeded kmeans ARI checks, 3) schedule 2% online A/B for 24h. I'll open tickets.

katie: thanks everyone. I'll update the staging run and open the rollout PR with the mixed-precision bundle and the gating rules.

mike: :thumbsup:

eva: uploaded full eval JSONs to the run and linked them in the doc. closing here unless someone needs more data.

alex: good work — let's reconvene after the A/B.

katie: closing thread.
